research_question: How do current-fed push-pull and closely related current-fed isolated converters redistribute conduction/switching loss, RMS and circulating current, semiconductor stress, magnetic burden and soft-switching range over wide input/load conditions?
metric_definition: No single scalar target; dimensions include efficiency curve, switch/diode stress, RMS current, circulating current, ZVS/ZCS coverage, magnetic structure and component burden
boundary_scope: isolated DC-DC front-end; low-voltage/high-current source to high-voltage DC output
topology_scope: current-fed push-pull; push-pull DAB; current-fed DAHB; closely related current-fed isolated front ends
input_voltage_scope: direct target 10-60 Vdc; 60-200 V context only unless deliberately re-scoped
output_voltage_scope: direct target approximately 300-450 Vdc when applicable
power_scope: direct target approximately 0.5-3 kW; 3-20 kW scaling/mechanism context
switching_frequency_scope: initial acquisition approximately 20-200 kHz; exact set may be narrowed after evidence density review
load_point_basis: efficiency curves or multiple matched load points preferred; light-load and full-load states typed separately
semiconductor_scope: primary and secondary controlled switches plus rectifier/commutation devices; measured/theory stress kept separate
auxiliary_loss_policy: direct efficiency ranking prohibited unless included/excluded auxiliary, gate-drive, fan/cooling and control losses are compatible
measurement_basis: physical hardware experiment required for numerical promotion
normalization_rule: stress normalized only to the same physical voltage boundary; RMS/current metrics require same definition; efficiency keeps exact operating point and boundary
admissible_mismatch: topology and power scale may differ in BOUNDED_TRADEOFF mode but must be tagged direct_target versus mechanism_context
prohibited_inference: no overall-best topology; no peak-vs-full-load ranking; no claim that soft switching alone caused efficiency difference; no search-miss gap
next_gate: Acquire and full-text-audit at least two independent direct-target families before L5 comparison admission

research_question: At a matched low-voltage DC to single-phase AC boundary, does stage integration reduce total conversion loss or redistribute burden into RMS current, magnetics, energy buffering, semiconductor stress and control?
metric_definition: Complete DC-input to AC-output boundary; stage efficiencies retained separately from total system efficiency
boundary_scope: low-voltage DC source -> isolated conversion -> optional DC link -> single-phase AC output
topology_scope: two-stage isolated DC-DC + inverter versus isolated single-stage/high-frequency-link alternatives
input_voltage_scope: direct target 10-60 Vdc; higher-voltage systems context unless normalized only for mechanism
output_voltage_scope: 110/220-230 Vac single phase; intermediate DC link recorded separately
power_scope: direct target approximately 0.5-2 kW; adjacent scales context
switching_frequency_scope: not fixed at discovery stage; switching frequencies must be recorded per stage
load_point_basis: same input voltage, output power and load basis required for any direct quantitative efficiency claim
semiconductor_scope: all power switches/diodes across the full system boundary; per-stage stress retained
auxiliary_loss_policy: end-to-end ranking requires compatible auxiliary/cooling/control-loss inclusion; stage-only efficiency cannot substitute
measurement_basis: physical complete-system hardware required for direct system comparison
normalization_rule: total loss may be expressed as W or loss per 100 W only when electrical boundaries match; stage efficiencies are not multiplied across incompatible or partial-power paths
admissible_mismatch: single-stage and two-stage topology differences allowed only as structured trade-off evidence unless full system boundary is matched
prohibited_inference: fewer stages does not imply higher efficiency; stage efficiency cannot be ranked against system efficiency; no Research Gap from missing comparator
next_gate: Populate system-level candidates and import conversation-audited full-text records only after repository provenance/locator restoration
